title: Review 3: Reed, cover, production and crimp

quizzes.title: Key terms across the lectures
quizzes.intro: The terms of the loom-side calculations.

questions.q: A dent is
options: One gap between two wires of the reed
questions.explain: Warp ends are drawn through the dents; dents per inch × ends per dent fixes the ends per inch in the reed.

questions.q: The Stockport sett of a reed is the number of dents in
questions.explain: With two ends per dent, the Stockport number is also the ends per inch in the reed.

questions.q: Relative cover of one set of threads is
questions.explain: d/p shows what fraction of the spacing each thread fills; at 1 the threads touch.

questions.q: In the mill form of cover factor, K for one set is
questions.explain: K = threads per inch ÷ √Ne; about 28 means the threads of that set touch.

questions.q: Crimp is
options: The extra length of yarn compared with the cloth it lies in
The size picked up by the warp
questions.explain: Crimp % = (yarn length − cloth length) ÷ cloth length.

questions.q: A jammed structure is one in which
options: The threads touch and cannot be packed closer
questions.explain: In Peirce’s jammed plain weave the yarn has no straight part; it is all arc.

questions.q: Loom efficiency is the share of time the loom is actually weaving.
questions.explain: Stops for warp and weft breaks and beam changes reduce efficiency below 100%.

questions.q: A core-spun stretch yarn has
options: An elastane filament in the centre with cotton wrapped around it
Polyester and cotton blended in the blowroom
questions.explain: The Lycra core gives stretch; the cotton sheath gives the look and feel.

questions.q: Fibre composition on a fabric label is stated by
questions.explain: It is the percentage by weight of each fibre in the whole fabric.

questions.q: A weave factor (divisor) is applied to twills and satins because they interlace less often and can be set denser than plain weave.
questions.explain: Dividing the cover factor by the weave factor gives a plain-weave equivalent to compare with the loom’s limit.

quizzes.title: Linking the ideas
quizzes.intro: How reed, cover, speed and crimp respond to a change.

questions.q: The ends per inch in the finished cloth are higher than in the reed because
questions.explain: The weft pulls the cloth narrower than the reed width, so the same ends sit in fewer inches.

questions.q: Changing from 2 to 4 ends per dent, for the same ends per inch, needs a reed with
options: Twice as many dents per inch
Half as many dents per inch
questions.explain: Ends per inch = dents per inch × ends per dent, so doubling ends per dent halves the dents needed.

questions.q: If a coarser yarn is used at the same threads per inch, the cover factor
questions.explain: A coarser yarn has a lower Ne, so threads ÷ √Ne is larger: thicker threads cover more.

questions.q: Cloth cover from warp cover C₁ and weft cover C₂ is
questions.explain: The product C₁C₂ is the area covered by both sets, which would otherwise be counted twice.

questions.q: A construction is easy to weave at 75 inches. On a 134 inch air-jet loom it may be unweavable because
options: Wider looms tolerate a lower cover factor
questions.explain: The pick must travel further, so the limit on total cover falls as the loom gets wider.

questions.q: Loom speed is unchanged but picks per inch rise from 50 to 60. Production in metres per day
questions.explain: Length per minute = rpm × efficiency ÷ PPI, so it falls to 50/60 = 83% of before.

questions.q: In a jammed plain weave, making the weft thicker than the warp makes the warp crimp
questions.explain: The warp must bend round a bigger crossing thread, so it follows a longer path.

questions.q: A 2/2 twill has less crimp than a plain weave of the same yarns, because each thread interlaces less often.
questions.explain: About 13% against 21% in the jammed state: floats are straight and add no crimp.

questions.q: In a warp rib with thick weft, the yarn consumption is unusual because
options: The weft crimp is very high
The warp crimp is very high while the weft lies almost straight
questions.explain: The warp wraps around the thick picks (about 57% crimp in the lecture) and the weft has almost none.

questions.q: Elastane is fed into core spinning under draft, so its share of the yarn is smaller than its nominal denier suggests.
questions.explain: A 40 denier filament drafted 4 times contributes only about 10 denier per unit length of yarn.

quizzes.title: Mixed calculations
quizzes.intro: Reed, cover, production, crimp and blend calculations.

questions.q: A reed has 1,260 dents per metre. How many dents per inch is that, to one decimal? (1 m = 39.37 in)
questions.explain: 1,260 ÷ 39.37 = 32.0 dents per inch.

questions.q: A reed has 30 dents per inch. What is its Stockport sett?
questions.explain: Stockport sett = dents per two inches = 60.

questions.q: A reed has 30 dents per inch, drawn 3 ends per dent. Weft contraction is 5%. What are the ends per inch in the cloth, to one decimal?
questions.explain: 30 × 3 = 90 in the reed; × 1.05 = 94.5 in the cloth.

questions.q: What is the warp cover factor of a cloth with 100 ends per inch of Ne 25?
A warp has a cover factor of 21. What is its relative cover in percent, taking 28 as full cover?
Warp cover is 0.80 and weft cover 0.50. What is the cloth cover, to two decimals?
A loom runs at 600 rpm with 90% efficiency, weaving 54 picks per inch. How many inches of cloth does it make per minute?
questions.explain: 600 × 0.9 ÷ 54 = 10 inches a minute.

questions.q: A loom makes 10 inches of cloth a minute. How many metres does it weave in 24 hours, to one decimal? (1 yd = 0.9144 m)
A yarn pulled out of 20.0 cm of cloth measures 21.8 cm when straightened. What is the crimp in percent?
A fabric has 0.25 lb of 100% cotton warp and 0.20 lb of 50/50 cotton-polyester weft in each yard. What is the polyester content of the fabric in percent, to one decimal?
questions.explain: Polyester = 0.10 lb of 0.45 lb = 22.2%.

quizzes.title: Case study
quizzes.intro: Is this twill weavable, which reed does it need and how fast will it come off the loom?

questions.q: How many ends per inch are there in the reed, to one decimal?
questions.explain: 128 in the cloth ÷ 1.05 = 121.9 in the reed.

questions.q: How many dents per inch must the reed have, to one decimal?
questions.explain: 121.9 ends per inch ÷ 4 ends per dent = 30.5.

questions.q: What is the reed count in dents per metre, to the nearest 10? (1 m = 39.37 in)
questions.explain: 30.48 × 39.37 ≈ 1,200; a 1,200 reed would be ordered.

questions.q: What is the width of the warp in the reed, in inches to two decimals?
What is the warp cover factor, to one decimal?
What is the weft cover factor?
What is the plain-equivalent total cover factor (warp plus weft, divided by the weave factor), to one decimal?
Comparing the plain-equivalent cover factor of about 33.6 with the loom’s limit of 36, the cloth is
options: Weavable, with a little room to spare
questions.explain: 33.6 is below 36, so the twill can be woven; as a plain weave (43.6) it could not.

questions.q: How many yards does the loom weave in 24 hours, to one decimal?
How many loom-days are needed to weave an order of 40,000 yards, to the nearest whole number?
questions.explain: 40,000 ÷ 396.7 yards per loom per day = 101 loom-days (for example 10 looms for about 10 days).

quizzes.case: A 3/1 twill, 20 × 16 / 128 × 60, is to be woven 63 inches wide on a 75 inch air-jet loom running at 700 rpm with 85% efficiency. It is drawn 4 ends per dent, and the cloth is 5% narrower than the warp in the reed (weft contraction). For a 3/1 twill the cover factor is divided by a weave factor of 1.3, and a 75 inch air-jet loom weaves comfortably up to a total plain-equivalent cover factor of 36.

quizzes.title: Group challenge
quizzes.intro: Harder questions that join cover, crimp, production and composition.

questions.q: In a jammed plain weave of equal yarns the thread spacing is p = 1.732 d and the yarn length per crossing is l = 2.094 d. What is the crimp in percent, to one decimal?
A cloth is 20 × 20 / 108 × 56. What is its total cover factor (warp plus weft), to one decimal?
A 2/2 twill has warp cover factor 30 and weft cover factor 17. Its weave factor is 1.34. What is the plain-equivalent cover factor, to one decimal?
A stretch yarn is Ne 30 (177 denier). Its core is 40 denier Lycra fed at a draft of 4, which then shrinks back 6%. What is the Lycra content of the yarn in percent, to one decimal?
An order of 50,000 m must be woven in 20 days. Each loom makes 400 m a day, of which 2% is B-grade. How many looms are needed (round up)?
questions.explain: A-grade per loom = 392 m a day, or 7,840 m in 20 days; 50,000 ÷ 7,840 = 6.4, so 7 looms.

questions.q: A fabric uses 0.27 lb of warp per metre. Allowing 3% wastage and 1% B-grade (divide by 0.99), how many 100 lb bags of warp yarn does a 60,000 m order need, to one decimal?
A warp is all cotton; the weft is 65/35 polyester-cotton and weighs the same as the warp. The fabric is
questions.explain: Only half the fabric weight is weft, and 65% of that half is polyester: 0.5 × 65% = 32.5%.

questions.q: Two cloths have the same total cover factor. One is plain weave and the other a 5-end satin. Which is harder to weave?
questions.explain: Plain interlaces at every thread. The satin’s cover factor is divided by its weave factor, giving a lower plain-equivalent figure.

questions.q: In Peirce’s jammed plain weave of equal yarns, the cover factor of each set (K = 1,542 on the tex scale) is below the maximum of 2,670 because crossing threads need room to pass between.
questions.explain: The threads of one set cannot touch each other when threads of the other set pass between them, so spacing is 1.732 d, not d.

questions.q: A reed of 60 Stockport is drawn 3 ends per dent for a twill instead of 2 for plain. The ends per inch in the reed become
questions.explain: 60 Stockport = 30 dents per inch; × 3 ends per dent = 90 ends per inch.
